issues.failure_explanation: Substituting x_j = u+iv and b_j = r+is into (A - λ_j I)x_j = b_j with λ_j = p+iq gives Ψu + qv = r and Ψv - qu = s, where Ψ = A - pI. The displayed saddle system instead enforces q u - Ψ v = -r and Ψ u - q v = s. These equations are not equivalent. For example, with A=2, λ=1+i, x=1+i, b=2, the displayed system gives [0;2]=[-2;0]. Thus the real system does not solve the original complex subproblem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:saddlesystem with the correct equivalent real system, e.g. [[q I, Ψ],[Ψ, -q I]] [Im x; Re x] = [Re b; Im b] for q>0, with appropriate sign handling for q<0.
issues.overall_effect: The entire saddle point reformulation and all P_SP numerical results and claims about solving the block problems are invalid.
issues.title: Saddle point reformulation is not equivalent to the complex shifted system
issues.why_classification: The central reformulation for the second preconditioning method is wrong; no version of the P_SP method as written is supported, and the numerical results based on it cannot be trusted. Repair requires rederiving the inner system and redoing the method's convergence and implementation.

issues.failure_explanation: For j in the second half of the complex roots (e.g. j ∈ [ℓ/2+2,ℓ]), Im(λ_j) is negative, so Φ = Im(λ_j)I is negative definite, not SPD. Consequently Φ+Ψ may not be SPD either, so the preconditioner P_D in eq:minresprecond is not guaranteed to be SPD and the AMG/MINRES assumptions are violated. The source later explicitly solves these negative-imaginary subproblems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the saddle point formulation to roots with positive imaginary part and handle negative-imaginary roots by conjugate symmetry, or use |Im(λ_j)| and swap/sign-adjust the variables and right-hand side.
issues.overall_effect: The P_SP method is not well-defined as stated for half of the complex subproblems; Theorem thm:added-2 cannot be applied to them, and their numerical results rely on an unstated workaround.
issues.title: Claimed SPD blocks fail for negative imaginary roots
issues.why_classification: A contained sign-handling fix (using conjugate pairs or |Im|) preserves the method, but the source as written applies an SPD preconditioner to indefinite blocks, invalidating the stated guarantees for those subproblems.

issues.failure_explanation: MINRES is a linear Krylov subspace method for symmetric (indefinite) linear systems; in exact arithmetic its solution is a linear function of the right-hand side. Calling it nonlinear is incorrect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove 'nonlinear' or state that MINRES is a linear Krylov method.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed contrast that the nested Chebyshev approach is 'completely linear' while the saddle point approach uses a 'nonlinear solver' is unsupported. This is a minor misstatement in the conclusions.
issues.title: MINRES is misclassified as a nonlinear solver
issues.why_classification: The error is a local misclassification in the conclusions; it does not affect any theorem, algorithm, or numerical result, and is corrected by a one-word change.
